## Problem

Nobody with read-only access to a cluster could tell which functions
nvsnap had cached, before or after a deploy:

- **The records** in `nvsnap-system` (`nvsnap-criu-group-<key>`,
  `nvsnap-cachedir-<key>`) decide every admission. Their names are a
  hash, and the only identity on them was `source`, the namespace and pod
  the capture was taken from. That namespace is deleted with the
  instance, and the function id goes with it.
- **The catalog** (`/api/v1/checkpoints` on nvsnap-server) lists every
  checkpoint ever made, failed and replaced ones too, by pod. It says
  nothing about what admission will do. Where the API server cannot reach
  the pod network, `kubectl get --raw …/proxy/…` times out, and a
  read-only user cannot port-forward.
- **`NvSnapFunctionState`** (`kubectl get nvsnapfunctionstates`) is
  NVCA's, from the NVCA-driven capture flow the webhook replaced. NVCA
  creates one per function version and almost none has a status. nvsnap
  must not write it: NVCA stamps `nvsnap.io/restore-from` on a version it
  sees `Warm`, which would bring back that restore path.

## Design

```
$ kubectl get nvsnapfunctions
NAME   FUNCTION   TENANT   STATE      METHOD     RANKS   VERIFIED   LAST-RESTORE-S   AGE
v-1    f-1        t-1      complete   criu       8       2h         42.5             3d
v-2    f-1        t-1      failed     cachedir   1                                   1d
v-3    f-9        t-2      capturing             2                                   5m
```

`kubectl get nvsnapfunctions -o wide` adds the reason; `-o yaml` has every
configuration of the version: its key, state, nodes, captures, the last
restores, restore failures, GPU faults, stalls, and its cachedir capture.
`-l nvsnap.io/function-id=<id>` lists one function's versions.

### 1. The record names its function version

A record's key is the configuration hashed with its scope, and the scope
is the function version (the namespace label `function-version-id`), or
the namespace outside NVCF (`criuGroupScope`). So a record belongs to
exactly one version, and two versions never share a capture.

The agents put the version's identity on the record as labels
(`fnstatus.Identity`), read from the namespace of the pod the record is
for:

| Label | From the namespace's |
|---|---|
| `nvsnap.io/function-version-id` | `function-version-id` (or `FUNCTION_VERSION_ID`) |
| `nvsnap.io/function-id` | `function-id` (or `FUNCTION_ID`) |
| `nvsnap.io/tenant` | the agent's tenant label (`agent.tenantLabel`) |
| `nvsnap.io/namespace` | its name |

- when a record is created or taken over for a capture
  (`claimGroupRecord`) or marked `gpushare-failed`;
- when admission finds a record (`lookupCRIUGroupFor`,
  `criuFallbackFor`): records made before the labels existed are named at
  their next admission. Admission that finds no record writes nothing;
- an alias names the record it points to as well;
- a merge patch on the labels only, so it never races a change of the
  record's data;
- off the caller's path, and at most once per record per agent per hour
  (once per five minutes after a failure); a failure is logged and never
  delays or fails an admission or a capture.

The labels are identity, not state: nothing nvsnap decides reads them.

### 2. The view

`NvsnapFunction` is a cluster-scoped CRD in the chart, one object per
version, named after the version id (`ns-<namespace>` outside NVCF).

nvsnap-server keeps them (`FunctionStatus`), like its rootfs-manifest
reconciler: every 30 seconds it lists the records and projects them
(`fnstatus.Project`):

- an object for every version a record names, created with its first
  record and deleted with its last (retired by the reaper, deleted by an
  operator). Not listed means nvsnap holds nothing for the version: its
  next pod starts cold;
- an object is written only when its status or labels change;
- a failed read of the records changes nothing: an empty list is never
  read as "nothing is cached";
- only objects the server made (`app.kubernetes.io/managed-by:
  nvsnap-server`) are updated or deleted;
- without the CRD the server logs once and carries on.

The server is one replica and already reads the cluster; the agents run
per node with no leader election. While the server is down the objects go
stale but stay readable; admission, capture and restore never read them.

**What the status says.** For each configuration, `state` is the record's
(`capturing`, `verifying`, `complete`, `failed`, `restore-failed`,
`gpushare-failed`), or `stalled` for a complete capture admission no longer
restores (its restores stalled `MaxStalls` times). `method` is how
admission starts the next pod: `criu` when it restores (the agent's
`parseCRIUGroup`: complete, or verifying for its own instance, not
stalled, a checkpoint for every rank), `cachedir` when a failed
configuration falls back to a complete cachedir capture, or empty for a
cold start. The top-level fields are the best configuration's: one that
restores, then one that falls back to the cachedir, then by state.
`TestFnstatusMatchesTheAgent` keeps the projection's names, states and
restore rule the agent's.

### 3. Read access

The chart adds a ClusterRole with `get`, `list` and `watch` on
`nvsnapfunctions`, aggregated into `view`, `edit` and `admin`: anyone who
can view the cluster can list them with no extra grant. Nothing secret is
in the objects: ids, node names, times and reasons.

The CRD is a template, not under `crds/`: Helm installs `crds/` on
install only, and a cluster upgraded to this chart needs it too. It is
kept on uninstall (`helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`).

### 4. Before a deploy

An object answers for a version nvsnap has seen. A new version of a
function has a new scope, so it starts cold and is captured on its own;
until then it is not listed.

## Why not

- **Write `NvSnapFunctionState`.** NVCA owns its schema and acts on
  `Warm` (see above). NVCA can stop creating it, or read `NvsnapFunction`
  instead; that is NVCA's change.
- **Stamp at every admission.** The webhook would write once per version
  per hour on the admission path. Naming the record where it is made, and
  where admission already finds it, writes once per record and keeps the
  admission path free of writes.
- **An index ConfigMap.** One object rewritten on every change, 1 MiB
  bound, no printer columns or label selection.
- **The catalog API.** Per checkpoint, not per function; it does not say
  what admission does; a read-only user cannot reach it.

## Limits

- A record made before this release is named at its next admission, and
  listed from then; one never admitted again is not listed.
- The view lags the records by up to 30 seconds.
- Per cluster, like the records.
- The status says what nvsnap will do at the next admission. It cannot
  promise the restore succeeds (a faulty GPU, a full node).

## Tests

- `internal/fnstatus`: the identity of NVCF and other namespaces and
  invalid values; the projection of each state, the restore rule, the
  cachedir fallback, the summary's order, aliases and unnamed records
  skipped, the bound on reasons.
- `internal/agent`: a record and the record its alias points to are
  named; a named record is not written again; a gone record is left
  alone; a record is read at most once an hour; a capture's record is
  named; `TestFnstatusMatchesTheAgent`.
- `internal/server`: an object is created with its version's first
  record, rewritten on a change and not otherwise, and deleted with the
  last record; others' objects are kept; a failed list deletes nothing;
  only the records' namespace and nvsnap's records are read; a status
  read back (int64) equals the one written (float64).
- Cluster: the CRD and the view role pass a server-side dry run. After
  install, a capture shows `capturing`, `verifying`, `complete` in turn,
  and a user bound only to `view` can list the objects.
